events.description: U.S. and Taliban sign the withdrawal agreement; the U.S. is to withdraw within 14 months, with a prisoner exchange and sanctions relief for Taliban figures.
U.S. goes to war in Afghanistan weeks after 9/11, after the Taliban refused to hand over bin Laden.
Mullah Omar dies; al-Qaeda maintains its oath to the Taliban emir.
al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent is founded to help the Taliban resurrect the Islamic Emirate.
Zawahiri swears allegiance to Mullah Mansour; the Taliban publish the acceptance in English on their website and later remove the page.
Mullah Mansour is killed in a U.S. drone strike in Pakistan.
Zawahiri renews his oath of allegiance to Hibatullah Akhundzada.
Khalilzad, then a private citizen, and Bill Roggio testify before a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee; Khalilzad calls Pakistan a state sponsor of terror.
Manba al-Jihad releases an hour-plus video, 'Bond of the Nation with the Mujahideen', celebrating the Taliban-al-Qaeda relationship.
During talks with the State Department, the Taliban release an English-subtitled video justifying the 9/11 attacks.
Asim Umar, found housed by a Taliban shadow governor, is killed in a joint U.S.-Afghan raid.
A New York Times op-ed is attributed to Sirajuddin Haqqani and does not mention al-Qaeda.
Recording date: 13-14 days after the agreement, with no Taliban disavowal of al-Qaeda and Taliban operations resumed in 27 of 34 provinces.

key_claims: The Feb 29, 2020 U.S.-Taliban agreement is a withdrawal deal rather than a peace deal, and it is lopsided in the Taliban's favor.
Al-Qaeda's bayah to the Taliban emir has been maintained from Omar through Mansour to Akhundzada, and the Taliban has not renounced it.
The Haqqani Network is an integral part of the Taliban command structure, closely tied to al-Qaeda, based in Pakistan and supported by the Pakistani military and ISI.
Pakistan has handed over no senior or mid-level Haqqani leaders, and the deal does not mention Pakistan despite Khalilzad's 2016 testimony.
Asim Umar, AQIS's first emir, was found living in a Taliban stronghold in Helmand and killed in September 2019, which the hosts cite as evidence against Taliban commitments.
AQIS was formed in 2014 to help the Taliban resurrect the Islamic Emirate, and the deal does not require the Taliban to act against it unless it plots against the West.
The deal has no verification or enforcement mechanisms, and no Taliban raids on al-Qaeda have been seen since signing.
The Taliban's July 2019 English-subtitled video justifying 9/11 shows it has not changed its stance.
